revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Cookie Houses
revealWordProblem.text:
A cookie house building kit contains three different cookie house kits. The finished houses are labeled A, B, and C, and the flat cookie pieces that fold up to make them are labeled 1, 2, and 3.
Question: Which flat kit matches which cookie house? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Three finished cookie houses labeled A, B, and C beside three flat nets labeled 1, 2, and 3.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Match each net to a house by counting and naming the faces. Count how many flat pieces each net has and what shape each one is, then check whether the finished house needs exactly those faces — a house with a peaked roof needs triangles, a box-shaped house needs six rectangles, and a pyramid-shaped house needs one base with triangles all around it. Fold each net mentally (or on paper) to confirm the pieces meet edge to edge with no overlap. The match is right when the number of faces, the shape of each face, and the way they fold all agree.

questions.stem: A rectangular prism has l = 6 in, w = 4 in, h = 2 in. What is its surface area?
choiceFeedback: Remember each face has a matching opposite face — double the sum of the three face areas.
That's the volume — surface area needs the sum of all six face areas, not length × width × height.
Check the units — surface area covers a flat surface, so it needs square units, not cubic.
hints: Surface area covers all 6 faces of the 6 × 4 × 2 box — it's not the same as the space inside.
Use SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh: find the three different face areas, double each, and add.
Start with the top face: 6 × 4 = 24 in². Then find 6 × 2 and 4 × 2 before doubling and adding.
questions.stemEs: Un prisma rectangular tiene l = 6 in, w = 4 in, h = 2 in. ¿Cuál es el área de su superficie?
hintsEs: El área superficial cubre las 6 caras de la caja de 6 × 4 × 2: no es lo mismo que el espacio de adentro.
Usa AS = 2la + 2lh + 2ah: halla las tres áreas de cara distintas, duplica cada una y suma.
Empieza con la cara de arriba: 6 × 4 = 24 pulg². Luego halla 6 × 2 y 4 × 2 antes de duplicar y sumar.

questions.stem: How many faces does a rectangular prism have?
questions.explanation: A rectangular prism has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, and right.
choiceFeedback: Don't forget the top and bottom — a box has faces all around it, not just the sides.
That's the number of corners (vertices), not the number of flat faces.
That's the number of edges, not the number of flat faces — count the flat surfaces instead.
hints: Picture a cereal box in your hands. Turn it: there's a front, a back, two sides, a top, and a bottom.
Count faces in opposite pairs — every face on a rectangular prism has a matching partner across from it.
Count the pairs: top/bottom is one pair, front/back is another, left/right is the third. Multiply pairs by 2.
questions.explanationEs: Un prisma rectangular tiene 6 caras: arriba, abajo, adelante, atrás, izquierda y derecha.
hintsEs: Imagina una caja de cereal en tus manos. Gírala: hay un frente, una parte trasera, dos lados, una tapa y una base.
Cuenta las caras en pares opuestos — cada cara de un prisma rectangular tiene una pareja igual del otro lado.
Cuenta los pares: arriba/abajo es un par, frente/atrás es otro, izquierda/derecha es el tercero. Multiplica los pares por 2.

questions.stem: Surface area is measured in which type of unit?
questions.explanation: Surface area measures flat surfaces, so it uses square units. Volume uses cubic units.
choiceFeedback: Cubic units measure 3D volume, not a flat surface — surface area needs a different kind of unit.
Linear units only measure length in one direction — surface area covers a flat region, needing two dimensions.
Every measurement needs a unit — think about what kind of unit matches a flat, two-dimensional surface.
hints: Surface area measures the flat covering on the outside of a solid — like wrapping paper.
Flat 2D measurements use square units. Save cubic units for filling space and plain units for length.
Imagine covering one face with 1-inch squares. Each square is 1 in² — that's the kind of unit surface area counts.
questions.stemEs: ¿Con qué tipo de unidad se mide el área de la superficie?
questions.explanationEs: El área de la superficie mide superficies planas, así que usa unidades cuadradas. El volumen usa unidades cúbicas.
hintsEs: El área superficial mide la cubierta plana del exterior de un sólido, como el papel de regalo.
Las medidas planas 2D usan unidades cuadradas. Guarda las cúbicas para llenar espacio y las simples para longitud.
Imagina cubrir una cara con cuadrados de 1 pulgada. Cada cuadrado es 1 pulg²: ese es el tipo de unidad que cuenta el área superficial.

steps: 1. A net is a 2D flat pattern that folds into a 3D solid without overlapping
2. Rectangular prism net has 6 rectangular faces in 3 congruent opposite pairs
3. Surface Area is the total sum of the areas of all flat faces on the net
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Surface Area Using Nets is finding the area of only one face from each of the 3 matching pairs and forgetting to double it, instead of counting all 6 faces. For a box that is 9 in × 4 in × 5 in, a student might add just one face from each pair: (9×4) + (9×5) + (4×5) = 36 + 45 + 20 = 101 in², but the net actually has two of each face, so the correct total is 2(36) + 2(45) + 2(20) = 72 + 90 + 40 = 202 in² — exactly double. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I count both matching faces in each pair, or only one from each pair?'

level2.explanation: A cube has 6 identical faces. Each face: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Total SA = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².
choiceFeedback: Square the edge length for one face's area first, then multiply by the number of faces.
That's the volume calculation (edge cubed) — surface area needs six face areas added together.
Check the units — a flat surface is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: A cube's 6 faces are identical squares, each one 5 cm by 5 cm.
Find the area of one square face, then multiply by 6 — and keep square units (cm²).
One face is 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Now multiply that area by the number of faces, 6.

level3.prompt: Two boxes have the same volume of 60 in³. Box A is 5 × 4 × 3. Box B is 10 × 6 × 1. Which box uses less wrapping paper (has less surface area)? Show your calculations and explain why a more cube-like shape might use less material.
level3.sentenceFrame: Box A: SA = 2(___) + 2(___) + 2(___) = ___ in². Box B: SA = 2(___) + 2(___) + 2(___) = ___ in². Box ___ uses less wrapping paper because ___.
level3.hint: Find the surface area of each shape, then compare the totals.
hints: Both boxes hold 60 in³, but wrapping paper depends on SURFACE AREA — the outside covering, not the inside space.
Compute SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh for each box, then compare the two totals before you explain.
Box A first: faces are 5×4 = 20, 5×3 = 15, and 4×3 = 12. Double each and add, then repeat for Box B's faces.
level3.explanation: Both boxes hold 60 in³, but wrapping paper is measured by surface area. Box A: 2(20) + 2(15) + 2(12) = 94 in². Box B: 2(60) + 2(10) + 2(6) = 152 in². Box A uses less paper because its dimensions are closer to a cube — flattening the same volume into 10 × 6 × 1 creates two huge 60 in² faces and a lot of extra covering.
